evidence.finding: Under msprof L1 the installed launcher inspects Tensor.size() on its pointer parameters. The cached fast-path launch in run() passes out_ptr/in_ptr Python ints from data_ptr() into those pointer slots, producing AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'size'. The identical wrapper is the transfer basis: the failure originated on the shared baseline and also applies to both experimental variants.

hypothesis: The failure is purely a host-wrapper compatibility issue in the cached launch call. The generated launcher accepts real tensor objects for pointer parameters (it only needs the raw address at non-profiling time), so passing the current-call `out` and `input` tensors instead of their data_ptr() integers keeps the raw addresses identical while letting msprof's tensor registration call size().
change: In run()'s cached launch path, pass `out` and `input` (the current call's tensor objects) in the two pointer parameter slots instead of `out_ptr` and `in_ptr`. Keep the current raw stream argument, the same launch metadata/grid/scalar arguments (`entry[3], 1, 1`), the same None placeholders, allocation, and all cache keys (which still use data_ptr() & 15 alignment). No kernel, grid, arithmetic, contract, reference, profiler, or runtime changes.
expected: The launcher receives tensors whose .size() is available under msprof L1, so the AttributeError disappears; launch addresses, grid and scalar specializations are unchanged, so kernel behavior and timing are byte-identical.
validation: Run the bridge preflight --source candidate.py on the edited file; confirm it is accepted (or awaiting_source_review, in which case source is retained). Kernels and device optimization remain byte-identical to the given source SHA.
